title: Linked references may carry their label after the link
summary: The `reference-without-label` writing lint previously only accepted a bracketed description sitting immediately after the reference text, so a reference wrapped in a Markdown link — the form the rule itself recommends — was flagged unless the label lived inside the link text. This change widens the check: a label directly after the link's closing bracket now counts too. The link spans are collected as whole-match ranges instead of capture group 1, and each reference is matched against the span that contains it so the text after the span's end can be inspected. Two tests pin the new pass case and confirm a bare linked reference still fails.

nodes.label: reference_without_label
nodes.subtitle: fn(&TextUnit, &WritingConfig) -> Vec<Finding>
nodes.summary: The rule under change. It masks code spans, collects Markdown link spans, then walks every `owner/repo#N` or `repo#N` occurrence. A reference now counts as labelled if a `(` follows either the reference itself or the end of the link span that contains it.

nodes.label: link span collection
nodes.summary: Previously captured group 1 of the link regex, which is the link text only. Now uses `find_iter` so each span covers the whole `[text](url)` match, which is what makes the closing bracket's position available to the label check.

nodes.label: label check
nodes.summary: The `labelled` predicate. It keeps the original `rest.trim_start().starts_with('(')` test on the text after the reference, and ORs in the same test applied to the text after the containing link span's end.

nodes.label: mask_ranges
nodes.subtitle: fn(&str, &[Range<usize>]) -> String
nodes.summary: Blanks out inline code spans before matching, so references inside backticks are never judged. Untouched by this change but on the path every reference takes.

nodes.label: finding
nodes.subtitle: builds a Finding at a span
nodes.summary: Constructs the emitted finding for an unlabelled reference. Called only when `labelled` is false, so the widened predicate directly reduces how often it runs.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: &[RuleMeta]
nodes.summary: The static rule table. The `reference-without-label` entry's "What it does" prose now says the description may also sit right after the Markdown link that wraps the reference, matching the new behaviour.

nodes.label: a_linked_reference_with_a_label_after_the_link_passes
nodes.summary: New test asserting no findings for an issue link and a pull request link each followed by `(the label)`.

nodes.label: a_linked_reference_without_a_label_still_fails
nodes.summary: New test asserting a linked reference with nothing after the closing bracket still yields `reference-without-label`, guarding against the rule being weakened into a no-op.

nodes.label: rules_of

nodes.summary: Test helper that runs the writing rules over a string and returns the fired rule names. Both new tests go through it.

edges.label: labelled?
